name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Classification of intrauterine devices and sterilization

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Non-medicated IUD I. Multiload 375
B. Copper-releasing IUD II. Lippes loop
C. Hormone-releasing IUD III. Tubectomy
D. Surgical sterilisation in females IV. Progestasert

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Contraceptive methods are categorized based on their structural design, chemical composition, and mechanism of action within the reproductive tract.

Step 2: Evaluation of Components
• Non-medicated intra-uterine devices do not release active ions or hormones; Lippes loop is the canonical example of a non-medicated IUD.
• Copper-releasing intra-uterine devices release copper ions into the uterine cavity; Multiload 375, CuT, and Cu7 belong to this class.
• Hormone-releasing intra-uterine devices release synthetic progestogens locally; Progestasert and LNG-20 are prominent examples.
• Surgical sterilisation in females involves the removal or ligation of a small section of the fallopian tubes, a procedure termed tubectomy.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Non-medicated IUD with Lippes loop, Copper-releasing IUD with Multiload 375, Hormone-releasing IUD with Progestasert, and Surgical sterilisation in females with Tubectomy.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Assisted reproductive technologies and their procedures

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. ZIFT I. Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube
B. GIFT II. Transfer of zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube
C. IUI III. Direct mechanical injection of a sperm into an ovum in the laboratory
D. ICSI IV. Artificial introduction of semen directly into the uterus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) include specialized clinical and laboratory interventions designed to overcome specific physiological barriers to conception.

Step 2: Evaluation of Procedures
• ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves in vitro fertilisation followed by the transfer of the zygote or an early embryo containing up to 8 blastomeres directly into the fallopian tube.
• GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) entails transferring an unfertilised ovum harvested from a donor female into the fallopian tube of a recipient who cannot produce ova but can support fertilisation and gestation.
• IUI (Intra-Uterine Insemination) is an artificial insemination method in which processed semen is introduced directly into the uterine cavity.
• ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is a microscopic procedure wherein a single sperm is injected directly into the cytoplasm of an ovum under laboratory conditions.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs ZIFT with transfer of zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube, GIFT with transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube, IUI with artificial introduction of semen directly into the uterus, and ICSI with direct mechanical injection of a sperm into an ovum in the laboratory.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Modes of action of contraceptive methods

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Copper-releasing IUDs I. Inhibit ovulation and alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent sperm entry
B. Hormone-releasing IUDs II. Suppress sperm motility and reduce the fertilising capacity of sperms
C. Oral contraceptive pills III. Mechanically block the entry of sperms through the cervix
D. Diaphragms and cervical caps IV. Make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different contraceptive devices and preparations function by disrupting specific reproductive events such as gamete transport, fertilisation competence, ovulation, or blastocyst implantation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Modes of Action
• Copper ions released from copper-bearing intra-uterine devices exert a direct spermicidal effect, suppressing sperm motility and significantly diminishing sperm fertilising capacity.
• Hormone-releasing intra-uterine devices continuously elute progestogens, which render the endometrium unsuitable for blastocyst implantation and make the cervical mucus hostile and impenetrable to sperms.
• Combined oral contraceptive pills contain progestogen-estrogen formulations that suppress gonadotropin secretion (inhibiting ovulation), prevent implantation, and alter cervical mucus consistency to retard sperm penetration.
• Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are rubber barrier devices placed over the uterine cervix to physically block sperms from entering the upper female reproductive tract.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Copper-releasing IUDs with suppression of sperm motility and reduction of fertilising capacity, Hormone-releasing IUDs with making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile, Oral contraceptive pills with inhibition of ovulation and alteration of cervical mucus, and Diaphragms and cervical caps with mechanical blocking of sperms through the cervix.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Operating principles of various contraceptive methods

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Periodic abstinence I. Interruption of gamete transport by cutting or tying the vas deferens
B. Lactational amenorrhea II. Physiological suppression of ovulation and menstrual cycle during intense suckling
C. Male condom III. Abstaining from coitus during day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
D. Vasectomy IV. Disposable latex sheath providing a barrier and protection against STIs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Contraception can be achieved through behavioural natural methods, mechanical barriers, or permanent surgical intervention by targeting the availability or passage of gametes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Methods
• Periodic abstinence relies on avoiding coitus during the fertile window (days 10 to 17 of the standard menstrual cycle), when ovulation is anticipated and fertilisation probability is highest.
• Lactational amenorrhea is rooted in the physiological fact that intense lactation post-parturition elevates prolactin, thereby inhibiting gonadotropin release, preventing ovulation and menstruation for up to 6 months.
• Condoms for males (such as Nirodh) are thin latex barriers that prevent semen deposition in the female tract and offer the dual advantage of protection against sexually transmitted infections.
• Vasectomy is a surgical sterilisation method in which a portion of each vas deferens is excised or ligated through the scrotum, blocking sperm transport into the ejaculate.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Periodic abstinence with abstaining from coitus during day 10 to 17 of the cycle, Lactational amenorrhea with suppression of ovulation during intense suckling, Male condom with disposable latex sheath providing barrier and STI protection, and Vasectomy with interruption of gamete transport via the vas deferens.

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Completely curable STI if detected early I. Hepatitis-B
B. Incurable viral STI II. Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
C. STI transmitted by sexual contact and shared needles III. Syphilis
D. Common complication of untreated STIs IV. Genital herpes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) vary in their etiology, curability, non-sexual transmission routes, and potential long-term pathological consequences.

Step 2: Evaluation of STI Characteristics
• Bacterial and protozoan STIs such as syphilis, gonorrhoea, and trichomoniasis can be completely cured if diagnosed early and treated appropriately with targeted antimicrobials.
• Among viral STIs, genital herpes, hepatitis-B, and HIV cannot be permanently eliminated or cured by current medical treatments.
• Hepatitis-B (and HIV) can be transmitted through sexual contact as well as parenteral routes including contaminated injection needles, blood transfusions, and vertical transmission from mother to foetus.
• Failure to detect and treat STIs early often leads to serious complications such as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, and infertility.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Completely curable STI with Syphilis, Incurable viral STI with Genital herpes, STI transmitted by sexual contact and shared needles with Hepatitis-B, and Common complication of untreated STIs with Pelvic inflammatory disease.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Milestones in reproductive health and family planning

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) I. Legalised in India with strict conditions to prevent female foeticide (1971)
B. National Family Planning Programme II. Developed the novel non-steroidal oral contraceptive Saheli in Lucknow
C. Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act III. Reported annual population growth rate of less than 2 per cent (20/1000/year)
D. 2011 Indian Census Report IV. Initiated at national level as an action plan in 1951

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India has historically undertaken national public health initiatives, legal frameworks, and research programmes to monitor demographics and ensure reproductive health.

Step 2: Evaluation of Milestones
• The Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) located in Lucknow, India, developed the non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill Saheli, taken once weekly.
• The national family planning programmes were officially launched by the Government of India in 1951, making India one of the first nations to establish such initiatives.
• The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act was passed in 1971 to legalise induced abortions under specified medical circumstances and prevent unsafe illegal abortions.
• The 2011 Census of India documented that the nationwide population growth rate was below 2 per cent (approximately 20 per 1000 individuals per year).

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs CDRI with development of the oral contraceptive Saheli in Lucknow, National Family Planning Programme with its initiation in 1951, MTP Act with its legalisation in 1971, and 2011 Census Report with reporting a growth rate of less than 2 per cent.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Barrier and chemical methods of contraception

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Nirodh I. Reusable female rubber barriers that cover the cervix during coitus
B. Vaults II. Popular male condom that protects against both pregnancy and STIs
C. Spermicidal creams and foams III. Non-steroidal once-a-week oral pill with high contraceptive value
D. Saheli IV. Chemical preparations applied along with barriers to enhance contraceptive efficacy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Contraceptive formulations and barrier products function through distinct physical occlusion, chemical spermicidal action, or selective pharmacological receptor modulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Products
• Nirodh is a widely distributed latex sheath (condom) for males that prevents semen deposition into the female tract and protects against STIs.
• Vaults, along with diaphragms and cervical caps, are reusable rubber barriers inserted into the female tract to cover the external os of the cervix.
• Spermicidal creams, jellies, and foams are chemical adjuncts containing surface-active agents that kill sperms, used in conjunction with barrier devices to boost efficiency.
• Saheli is an oral contraceptive tablet containing a non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator taken on a once-a-week schedule after initial loading.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Nirodh with the male condom protecting against STIs, Vaults with reusable female barriers covering the cervix, Spermicidal creams and foams with chemical preparations enhancing barrier efficacy, and Saheli with the non-steroidal once-a-week pill.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Infertility indications and assisted reproductive techniques

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Male partner unable to inseminate or having oligospermia I. Gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT)
B. Female unable to produce ova but possessing receptive fallopian tube and uterus II. Intra uterine transfer (IUT)
C. In vitro derived embryo with more than 8 blastomeres III. Intra-uterine insemination (IUI)
D. Laboratory technique where sperm is directly injected into ooplasm IV. Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The clinical choice of an Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) depends strictly on the exact anatomical, physiological, or gametogenic cause of infertility.

Step 2: Evaluation of Indications and Techniques
• When the male partner has erectile dysfunction preventing insemination or presents with severely low sperm count (oligospermia), semen from the husband or donor is concentrated and delivered directly into the uterus via intra-uterine insemination (IUI).
• When a female patient suffers from anovulation or ovarian failure but retains patent fallopian tubes and a normal uterine environment, an ovum from a healthy donor is transferred into her fallopian tube via gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT).
• In an in vitro fertilisation program, when culture in the laboratory proceeds beyond the 8-cell stage (more than 8 blastomeres), physiological timing dictates transfer into the uterine cavity, known as intra uterine transfer (IUT).
• When sperm counts or fertilising capacity are severely compromised, a single sperm is directly microinjected into the oocyte cytoplasm through intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Male partner unable to inseminate or having oligospermia with Intra-uterine insemination, Female unable to produce ova but possessing receptive organs with Gamete intra fallopian transfer, In vitro embryo with more than 8 blastomeres with Intra uterine transfer, and Laboratory sperm injection into ooplasm with Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Contraceptive delivery methods and administration regimens

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Combined oral steroid pills I. Inserted in the uterine cavity by medical personnel for long-term reversible contraception
B. Subdermal implants II. Daily intake for 21 days starting within first 5 days of cycle, followed by a 7-day pill-free interval
C. Emergency post-coital contraceptives III. Progestogen formulations placed beneath the skin providing multi-year sustained release
D. Copper T (CuT) IV. Administration of progestogens or IUD insertion within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Contraceptive regimens differ markedly in route of administration, dosage frequency, and time window of therapeutic action relative to coital exposure.

Step 2: Evaluation of Regimens
• Standard oral contraceptive pills follow a cyclical 28-day regimen: daily administration for 21 consecutive days (initiating within the first 5 days of menses) followed by a 7-day pill-free interval during which withdrawal bleeding occurs.
• Subdermal implants consist of silastic rods containing progestogens inserted beneath the skin of the upper arm, releasing hormones steadily to maintain contraception over several years.
• Emergency post-coital interventions require administration of progestogen pills, combined pills, or insertion of an IUD within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse or barrier failure to prevent conception.
• Copper T (CuT) is an intra-uterine device inserted non-surgically through the cervix into the uterine cavity by trained physicians or nurses, providing extended contraception.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Combined oral steroid pills with daily intake for 21 days with a 7-day gap, Subdermal implants with progestogens placed beneath the skin for sustained release, Emergency post-coital contraceptives with administration within 72 hours of intercourse, and Copper T with insertion in the uterine cavity by medical personnel.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Medical termination of pregnancy legal criteria

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Amniocentesis I. Requires the concurring opinion of two registered medical practitioners
B. MTP termination within first 12 weeks II. Karyotyping of fetal cells to diagnose Down syndrome or haemophilia
C. MTP termination between 12 and 24 weeks III. Requires the opinion of one registered medical practitioner formed in good faith
D. Global annual MTP volume IV. Approximately 45 to 50 million induced abortions (accounting for 1/5th of all conceived pregnancies)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Clinical foetal diagnosis and legal abortion guidelines in India are governed by strict medical criteria and statutory regulations established by the MTP Amendment Act.

Step 2: Evaluation of Guidelines and Statistics
• Amniocentesis is a foetal diagnostic test where amniotic fluid containing desquamated foetal cells is analysed to identify chromosomal anomalies like Down syndrome or genetic disorders such as haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia.
• Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act 2017, a pregnancy may be legally terminated during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks) on the opinion of a single registered medical practitioner.
• If pregnancy duration is between 12 and 24 weeks, the law mandates that two registered medical practitioners must independently concur in good faith that eligible statutory grounds exist.
• Across the world, approximately 45 to 50 million medical terminations of pregnancy are conducted each year, representing about one-fifth (20%) of all conceived pregnancies globally.

Step 3: Final Answer
Therefore, the correct association pairs Amniocentesis with karyotyping of fetal cells for genetic disorders, MTP termination within first 12 weeks with opinion of one registered practitioner, MTP termination between 12 and 24 weeks with opinion of two registered practitioners, and Global annual MTP volume with 45 to 50 million induced abortions.
